served.stem: 1-Hexyne is subjected to the following sequence: (1) NaNH2; (2) CH3CH2Br; (3) H2, Lindlar's catalyst. Which structure is the final major product?
served.bankWhy: Steps 1-2 alkylate the C6 acetylide with ethyl (C2) to give 3-octyne; step 3 (Lindlar) does syn reduction to cis (Z)-3-octene. Trans needs Na/NH3; octane is over-reduced; [3] is the alkyne (skipped Lindlar); [4] is cis-2-octene (wrong position).

answer.line: NaNH2 makes the acetylide, ethyl bromide adds two carbons, and Lindlar adds H2 to one face and stops: cis-oct-3-ene.

steps: Start with the acidic H. The terminal C-H of 1-hexyne, pKa about 25, goes to NaNH2 and leaves an acetylide anion.
The acetylide does SN2 on CH3CH2Br and adds two carbons: oct-3-yne, with the triple bond three carbons from the ethyl end.
Lindlar's poisoned catalyst adds both H to one face and quits at the alkene. One face means cis.

choices.note: Cis and eight carbons are right, but the C=C sits at C2, with one carbon on the short side. Ethyl bromide puts two carbons there, so the C=C sits at C3.
Octane is what plain H2 with Pd or Pt gives: two additions. Lindlar is poisoned so it stops after one.
This is the product of steps 1 and 2. Step 3 has not touched it yet.
Two carbons added, then one H2 to one face: cis at C3.
Trans comes from sodium in liquid ammonia. Lindlar gives cis.

student.lockIt: Lindlar stops at the cis alkene; sodium in ammonia stops at trans; H2 with Pd goes on to the alkane.
